SourcesBox score, game stories and the drawn play

Box score from the Thunder's 125–103 road win over the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center on Nov 15, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, matched line for line by the CBS Sports box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via KRMG and Yahoo Sports), Field Level Media (via Yardbarker), The Oklahoman, Sactown Sports, The Kings Herald and BVM Sports. All 125 Oklahoma City points and all 103 Sacramento points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (32–30–32–31 to 24–26–30–23) add up to both totals: 62–50 Oklahoma City at the half and 94–80 after three. Team totals (field goals 46 of 88 to 37 of 82, threes 10 of 31 to 14 of 43, free throws 23 of 28 to 15 of 20, steals 15–9, points in the paint 58–42) and the biggest leads (Oklahoma City 27, Sacramento 2) are from Covers; the 26 points off turnovers are from Field Level Media. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games: Oklahoma City 9–5 and 7th in the West, Atlanta 8–6.

Oklahoma City scored 17 of the first 21 points (Field Level Media); Sacramento tied it 47–47 late in the second quarter before the Thunder closed the half on a 15–3 run (AP). The Thunder opened the fourth quarter 19–6 to lead 113–86 with 7:01 left (Sactown Sports; the CBS play-by-play agrees), and Gilgeous-Alexander sat the whole fourth with 37 points (AP). It was his third straight 30-point game (Field Level Media). The win snapped Oklahoma City's three-game losing streak; Sacramento has lost six straight, is 1–12 and 0–8 at home (AP; Field Level Media). Rookie Aday Mara had 16 points and 13 rebounds off the bench (AP). Oklahoma City hosts Atlanta on Wednesday, Nov 18 at 8:00 PM ET; Sacramento hosts Phoenix the same night (Ball Exclusives; The Oklahoman).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's 3-pointer, assisted by Bennett Stirtz, that gave the Thunder a 91–76 lead with 1:44 left in the third quarter (AP; the CBS play-by-play calls it a pull-up jump shot and has Keegan Murray's three to make it 88–76 on the play before). The Oklahoman describes Gilgeous-Alexander answering Murray on the very next play. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's listed 6-foot-6 and 195 pounds with No. 2 (Wikipedia), arms scaled to the 6-foot-11½ wingspan measured at the 2018 draft combine (A Sea of Blue), in Oklahoma City's road blue with his approved look. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
